correctness.rationale: A recursive largest-gap split leaves two ordered children whose total span is at most (1-c0) times the parent span. Combining the resulting geometric decay of total active span with binary branching gives the exact exponent log 2 / log(2/(1-c0)); letting c0 increase to the optimal chain constant yields the bound. Central two-branch Cantor sets attain equality, and the explicit pure-jump clock has exactly that Cantor set as its image.

originality.rationale: The motivating Stieltjes-clock preprint identifies the optimal uniform-disconnectedness constant with kappa_g but contains no Assouad-dimension discussion. Targeted searches of uniform disconnectedness, porosity, Assouad dimension, sharp constants, chain bottlenecks, largest gaps, Cantor extremizers, and the explicit candidate formula found qualitative equivalences and general quantitative porosity bounds but no matching sharp one-dimensional extremal theorem or clock transfer.

value.rationale: The theorem gives the exact extremal tradeoff between a natural separation invariant and Assouad dimension on the line, identifies sharp Cantor extremizers for every parameter, and converts a new Stieltjes jump-dominance criterion into both a sharp dimension ceiling and a dimension-only characterization of universal Hölder selection.
